title: Wave-U-Net: A Multi-Scale Neural Network for End-to-End Audio Source Separation

citations.claim: Stoller et al. proposed Wave-U-Net, a one-dimensional adaptation of the U-Net architecture that performs audio source separation directly in the time domain, avoiding fixed spectral transformations and enabling end-to-end learning of phase information.
Wave-U-Net computes multi-scale features by repeatedly downsampling and upsampling 1D feature maps, combining high-level and low-level features at different time scales via skip connections.

Stoller et al. demonstrated that operating directly on raw waveforms avoids dependence on STFT hyperparameters such as window size and overlap, which affect time-frequency resolution and are typically fixed rather than optimized.
Stoller et al. introduced a difference output layer that enforces source additivity by computing the last source as the difference between the mixture and the sum of the other estimated sources.
Stoller et al. replaced strided transposed convolutions with linear interpolation followed by normal convolution for upsampling, avoiding high-frequency aliasing artifacts in the generated output.

Wave-U-Net showed that providing additional input context beyond the output prediction window avoids artifacts at output segment boundaries, which arise when zero-padding is used instead of proper temporal context.
Wave-U-Net achieved singing voice separation performance comparable to a state-of-the-art spectrogram-based U-Net architecture when trained under comparable settings.

do_not_claim: Wave-U-Net was applied to baseline correction or chromatographic signal processing
Wave-U-Net uses algorithm unrolling or iterative optimization
Wave-U-Net outperformed all spectrogram-based methods at the time of publication
